top_posts.text:
You just sent twelve euros to a merchant in Guangzhou whose name you can't read, under a contract you didn't open, in a jurisdiction where you'll never set foot. If the parcel never arrives, your legal recourse is, practically speaking, none — and both of you know it.

By Hobbes's logic, this trade should be impossible. Hundreds of millions of people do it weekly, and it works just fine.

It worked four thousand years ago too: Assyrian merchants at the karum of Kanesh ran contracts, joint-capital funds, and their own merchant court in 1900 BC — before commercial law existed anywhere. Wherever trade appears, the same toolkit appears: escrow, reputation, arbitration. Palaces differ; the merchant's toolkit does not.

The last essay I wrote with @1eyedgiantwalls, on builders and rulers, drew the best objection I've received in years, pressed over several rounds by a reader who wouldn't let go, Aleksander Szeser. This essay is our answer, and he wins a piece of it. From Kanesh to Champagne to Silk Road to Temu, and to the paradox of oil states: why order grows wherever people trade — and compounds only where no one can forbid it.

Europe's miracle was never its kings. It was the gaps between their umbrellas. Keep a border within reach.

top_posts.translation_zh:
你刚刚把十二欧元汇给了广州的一位商家，他的名字你都读不懂；依据的是一份你没有打开过的合同；所在的司法管辖区你这辈子都不会踏足。如果包裹永远不到，实际上你几乎没有任何法律救济——而你们双方都知道这一点。

按照霍布斯的逻辑，这种交易本应不可能发生。数以亿计的人每周都在这样做，而且运行得很好。

四千年前也是如此：公元前 1900 年，Kanesh 的 karum 中的亚述商人就已经在运行合同、联合资本基金和他们自己的商人法庭——那时任何地方都还没有商法。哪里出现贸易，哪里就会出现同一套工具：托管、声誉、仲裁。宫殿各不相同；商人的工具箱却不变。

我上一篇与 @1eyedgiantwalls 合写的文章，关于建设者与统治者，引出了我多年来收到的最佳反驳；一位不肯放手的读者 Aleksander Szeser 经过几轮反复追问提出了它。这篇文章就是我们的回答，而他赢得了其中的一部分。从 Kanesh 到 Champagne，到 Silk Road，到 Temu，再到石油国家的悖论：为什么秩序会在任何有人交易的地方生长——并且只会在无人能禁止它的地方复利增长。

欧洲的奇迹从来不是它的国王。奇迹在于他们保护伞之间的缝隙。让边境保持在触手可及之处。

@OpenAI’s ChatGPT web just “confessed” the exact execution-path split we kept running into while building VOOL:

SOL 5.6 in Codex/ChatGPT via ChatGPT login ≠ SOL 5.6 via API key.
Same model label. Different execution path—and, in our repeated real-world testing, materially different output quality.

“Third-brother mode”** is real enough to measure.

That means a model name alone tells you very little. The app, endpoint, harness, context handling and hidden limits can change the actual product you get.

@AnthropicAI users: are you seeing the same split between Claude App and API/CLI? We haven’t noticed it ourselves so far.

**Same model badge. Temu-grade execution path.
